newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Niaga down on profit-taking, S&P news.
newsitem.headline: Niaga down on profit-taking, S&P news.

text.p: Shares of Indonesia's privately-owned PT Bank Niaga fell in late Wednesday trading amid reports that Standard & Poor's may cut the bank's ratings, brokers said.
Bank Niaga fell 100 rupiah to 7,650 rupiah in late trading, with some one million shares traded. It recovered to close at 7,700 rupiah.
"The possible ratings downgrade prompted the profit-taking," one broker said.

Bank Niaga made sharp gains earlier this week on news that privately-owned PT Tunasmas Paduarta, a unit of the Tirtamas Group, planned to acquire a 50 percent stake in the bank at 8,000 rupiah per share.
Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday it had placed the BB long-term and single-B short-term ratings of Bank Niaga on creditwatch with negative implications.

It said Tirtamas, a diversified conglomerate, had indicated it intended to achieve economies of scale in the finance sector through the acquisition of the Bank Niaga stake, which might affect Bank Niaga's business profile.
Tirtamas own large stakes in various other Indonesian banks and in a leading insurance venture.
